title: Drugs that dismantle established pathogenic protein conformations and restore function

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a drug that acts on a harmful protein shape already established in human tissue, dismantles or neutralizes it, and enables sustained recovery of the function associated with that pathology. The intended result includes a clinically meaningful improvement in how a person functions. Changing a protein measurement or slowing further deterioration would not, by itself, demonstrate this restorative capability.

Early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease provides a documented motivation. The supplied Cochrane review reports that successful removal of amyloid from the brain does not seem to produce clinically meaningful effects in people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease. That finding identifies a gap between removal and clinical benefit in this setting. It does not establish that restorative pharmacology is absent across every disease involving abnormal protein conformations.

Conceptual scope: the therapeutic target is the pathogenic conformation—the harmful structural state of a protein—which a measurement of total deposited protein may not adequately distinguish. Dismantling that state, rendering it harmless, preventing additional deposition, and suppressing production are different interventions. PHA-07 centers on treating pathology that is already present and demonstrating recovery afterward; prevention before deposition addresses a different stage.

significance.text: A treatment that combined removal of established pathogenic conformations with sustained, clinically meaningful functional recovery would establish a substantial therapeutic capability beyond the limited clinical effects reported in the supplied Alzheimer’s review. The direct consequence would be evidence that treatment after deposition can recover useful function, rather than merely alter pathology measurements or slow functional decline. The review motivates that goal but does not demonstrate its achievement.

Conditional significance: recovery could matter wherever affected cells retain a capacity to function once the pathogenic state is controlled. However, removing deposited protein does not automatically repair damaged cells, replace lost neurons, or establish that the targeted conformation was the sole cause of impairment. Functional restoration must be measured directly, and the extent of recovery could depend on the tissue and disease stage. The supplied evidence does not determine those boundaries.

Conditional downstream possibility: success in another conformation disease would support transferability of the therapeutic principle. It would not establish one universally effective drug, a common mechanism across all proteinopathies, or recovery after every degree of tissue damage. Stopping protein production might complement treatment of existing pathology, but its restorative effects are not assessed by the supplied evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The documented challenge is to connect control of established pathology with meaningful clinical improvement. In the reviewed Alzheimer’s population, amyloid removal and the desired functional result have not aligned: the authors judged clinical effects insufficiently meaningful, with functional effects small at best. This supports a need to demonstrate restoration directly, while leaving open whether other mechanisms, disease stages, or conformation diseases could produce a different result.

Engineering synthesis: a candidate treatment would need to reach the affected tissue, engage the relevant pathogenic structural state, and dismantle or neutralize it safely. A corresponding measurement problem is to distinguish that state from bulk protein deposition where the two differ. These are requirements to resolve for a particular treatment, rather than barriers whose severity or universality has been established by the supplied source.

Scientific synthesis: the central unresolved questions concern what remains recoverable after pathology is controlled and how to attribute any improvement. A trial must distinguish sustained recovery from symptomatic fluctuation and from a slower rate of loss. Concurrent clearance and improvement would demonstrate a valuable therapeutic combination, but additional mechanistic evidence would be needed to show that clearance itself caused recovery. The supplied evidence does not resolve the contributions of persistent cellular damage, cell loss, or other disease processes.

current_state.text: Nonino and colleagues’ Cochrane review, published on 16 April 2026, examined amyloid-beta-targeting monoclonal antibodies in people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease. Its searches extended through 7 August 2025. At 18 months, the supplied evidence review reports a standardized mean difference of −0.11 for cognitive function, with moderate-certainty evidence, and −0.12 for dementia severity, with low-certainty evidence. The authors interpreted these findings as little to no difference in those outcomes.

Functional effects were small at best, with some scales showing small benefits. These findings should not be flattened into a claim of exactly zero benefit. They also do not demonstrate sustained functional recovery. The authors concluded that successful amyloid removal did not seem to be associated with clinically meaningful effects in the reviewed population, and reported that the antibodies increased the risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities.

The demonstrated scope is the reviewed antibody treatments and Alzheimer’s population. The findings do not establish failure of every clearance mechanism, a future non-antibody treatment, or treatment of other proteinopathies. The supplied abstract also does not quantify the original claim of large biomarker changes or establish that deposited amyloid alone caused the functional losses. Its evidence supports the narrower clearance–clinical benefit gap.

The retained source is a PubMed abstract record. The supplied review verified its identity and relevant abstract passages, but did not inspect the full Cochrane review or its figures. Although the source index records an untruncated extraction without extraction issues, that does not provide full-review coverage. The publication and search dates bound the findings: comprehensive coverage of developments through 1 November 2026 has not been established. These limitations restrict interpretation without showing that the reported results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: conduct a controlled human trial enrolling people with established deposits in a conformation disease. Demonstrate both removal of the pathogenic conformation on a validated direct tissue or imaging measure and a pre-specified, clinically meaningful functional gain. The functional result should show improvement, rather than only a slower rate of deterioration, over a period sufficient to distinguish sustained recovery from symptomatic fluctuation. These are proposed criteria, not established clinical or regulatory standards; the supplied evidence provides no numerical recovery threshold or required duration.
completion_criteria.label: Conformation removal and sustained clinically meaningful functional recovery in humans

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement and attribution requirements: show that the tissue or imaging measure represents the pathogenic conformation, particularly when bulk deposited protein is an imperfect proxy. Concurrent removal and recovery would demonstrate the therapeutic capability, while attributing recovery specifically to removal would require additional mechanistic evidence. Because the concept also includes neutralization, a treatment that leaves deposits present would need a separately justified measure showing that the harmful structural state or its pathogenic activity had been neutralized.
completion_criteria.label: Validated measures identify pathogenic conformation removal or justified neutralization

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independently replicate the combined pathological and functional result, report its durability and adverse effects, and define the disease stages and patient groups in which benefit occurs. Replication in a second conformation disease would support transferability. A single biomarker-positive antibody study would not establish restoration, and finite demonstrations would establish breadth only within the conditions tested, not literal universality across proteinopathies.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication reports durability, adverse effects, and defined benefit boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PHA-01, “A design method for pharmacological control of proteins that lack a usable binding pocket,” overlaps with the challenge of engaging a difficult protein target. It concerns a method for obtaining pharmacological control; PHA-07 requires control of established pathogenic conformations together with functional recovery. Solving target engagement would not by itself demonstrate the restorative outcome.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-05, “Systemic pharmacological access to brain parenchyma for arbitrary drug classes,” could enable brain-directed versions of PHA-07. PHA-11, “Reliable oral systemic exposure for folded peptides and proteins,” could improve delivery for a treatment using those modalities. Both concern access or exposure, whereas PHA-07 concerns what treatment accomplishes after reaching its target. Neither delivery capability alone establishes removal or recovery.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-06, “In-place pharmacological replacement of missing human cell types,” and PHA-12, “A pharmacological trigger for scarless regrowth of complex adult mammalian structures,” overlap with recovery when tissue damage includes missing cells or structures. PHA-07 focuses on pathogenic protein conformations. Replacement or regrowth could become complementary requirements where controlling those conformations leaves damage that surviving tissue cannot overcome.

Roster-based synthesis: PHA-02, “Prospective prediction of human efficacy, dose, and major toxicity before first-in-human exposure,” could help select and develop restorative candidates. PHA-13, “A medicine that holds its own therapeutic window without an external controller,” could help maintain effective and tolerable treatment. Their endpoints remain distinct from demonstrating recovery after established conformational pathology. PHA-09, “A drug that changes the human aging rate across organ systems,” has a broader cross-organ objective; recovery in one proteinopathy would not establish a change in the human aging rate.

change_log.change: Preserved PHA-07’s identity and restorative objective while narrowing the documented gap to the reviewed Alzheimer’s treatments and population.
change_log.reason: The supplied source supports that example but does not establish absence of restorative pharmacology across every conformation disease.

change_log.change: Replaced descriptions of trivial effects or cognition being almost unchanged with the review’s outcome-specific interpretation, quantitative estimates, certainty levels, and acknowledgment of small benefits on some functional scales.
change_log.reason: This preserves the limited clinical result without implying exactly zero benefit or sustained recovery.

change_log.change: Separated biomarker change, slower clinical decline, and functional improvement.
change_log.reason: The original wording conflated a clinical trajectory with a biomarker outcome.

change_log.change: Qualified claims about years-long persistence across multiple diseases, large biomarker changes, and benefits from suppressing protein production.
change_log.reason: Those assertions are not established by the supplied abstract; their uncertainty does not invalidate the proposed innovation.

change_log.change: Integrated distinctions between pathogenic conformations and bulk deposits, therapeutic demonstration and causal attribution, and removal and neutralization.
change_log.reason: Target measurements must represent the harmful state, and concurrent clearance and recovery alone do not establish causation. Neutralization also needs a measurement pathway consistent with the concept.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed completion criteria to address reproducibility, durability, safety, and disease-stage boundaries, while retaining second-disease replication as evidence of transferability.
change_log.reason: These proposals make the demonstration more convincing without presenting them as published standards or treating finite tests as proof of universality.

change_log.change: Added the publication date, search cutoff, abstract-only access boundary, and unverified coverage through November 2026.
change_log.reason: The dated findings remain assessable, but neither the source extraction nor its retrieval date establishes full-review access or comprehensive freshness.

change_log.change: Explained relevant relationships to the supplied roster without merging concepts.
change_log.reason: Target engagement, delivery, prediction, regeneration, and therapeutic-window control may support PHA-07 while retaining distinct objectives.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether another conformation disease or drug mechanism has already demonstrated the combined restorative capability.
The full Cochrane review and its figures were not inspected in the supplied review; details beyond the reviewed abstract remain unassessed.
Developments after the review’s 7 August 2025 search cutoff are not comprehensively accounted for, so field-wide openness as of 1 November 2026 remains unverified.
No disease-specific functional threshold, follow-up duration, or validated pathogenic-conformation assay is supplied for the proposed demonstration.
A neutralization-based treatment needs a justified measure of loss of pathogenic activity when deposits remain present; removal-based criteria alone would not cover that route.
The mechanistic evidence needed to attribute recovery specifically to conformation removal or neutralization remains to be defined.
The recoverability of affected tissue, the contribution of cell loss or other pathology, and the need for complementary replacement or regeneration remain unresolved.
No substantive review recommendation was rejected; the additional neutralization and reproducibility criteria are explicitly identified as proposals.

brief.title: Drugs that clear harmful proteins and restore function
possible: People whose organs are impaired by harmful protein shapes could regain useful function after the damage has begun. A drug would dismantle those shapes or make them harmless, with recovery that lasts.
why: For people with diseases involving harmful protein deposits, success would mean recovering abilities after deposits have formed. It would move treatment beyond changing a scan or slowing further loss.

sources.showed: Their review of drugs targeting amyloid-beta protein deposits in early Alzheimer’s disease found little to no difference in thinking or dementia severity. Benefits in daily functioning were small at best.
sources.quote: Amyloid-beta-targeting monoclonal antibodies may result in little to no difference in dementia severity
sources.cited_for: Removing protein deposits does not necessarily deliver meaningful clinical improvement.
sources.not_established: These treatments did not demonstrate sustained functional recovery, but their results do not settle what other treatments or diseases could achieve.

sources.showed: In a small early human trial, NI006 appeared to reduce scan measurements used to estimate harmful protein deposits in the heart. No apparent serious side effects were attributed to the drug.
sources.quote:
The use of NI006 was associated with no apparent drug-related serious adverse 
events.
sources.cited_for: Treatment may reduce established protein deposits in the human heart.
sources.not_established: Indirect scan measurements do not establish removal of the harmful protein shape together with sustained, meaningful functional recovery.

sources.showed: In an uncontrolled trial involving 23 people, miridesap followed by dezamizumab cleared protein deposits from several organs. Liver blood tests improved alongside clearance from the liver.
sources.quote:
Progressive dose-related clearance of hepatic 
amyloid was associated with improved liver function tests.
sources.cited_for: Established deposits can be cleared in humans alongside improvements in tests of organ function.
sources.not_established: Better liver blood tests in an uncontrolled trial do not establish sustained, meaningful recovery in how people function.

sources.showed: An early human trial of NEOD001 in people with protein deposits and persistent organ dysfunction reported heart and kidney responses in some patients.
sources.cited_for: Treatment aimed at harmful proteins has produced signs of organ improvement.
sources.not_established: Reported organ responses do not establish removal of the harmful protein shape together with sustained, meaningful functional recovery.

shown: Richards and colleagues linked clearance of established deposits to better liver blood tests. Garcia-Pavia and colleagues found signs of reduced heart deposits. These early results connect treatment to changes in organs, but do not yet demonstrate the full combination of clearance and lasting functional recovery.
missing: A controlled human trial would need to demonstrate removal of established harmful protein shapes alongside meaningful functional gains that last.
Validated measurements would need to distinguish the harmful shape from total deposits, or show that remaining deposits have become harmless.
Independent teams would need to reproduce recovery and establish its duration, side effects and limits across patient groups.

milestones.label: Protein removal and lasting functional recovery in humans
milestones.explanation: A controlled human trial would have to show removal of established harmful protein shapes and a meaningful functional gain that lasts. This would demonstrate recovery beyond slower deterioration.

milestones.label: Measurements confirm removal or loss of harmful activity
milestones.explanation: Validated tests would have to identify removal of the harmful shape, or loss of its harmful activity if deposits remain. This would distinguish control of the disease target from a change in total protein.

milestones.label: Independent confirmation establishes durability, side effects and benefit boundaries
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce the combined result and report durability, harms and who benefits. Success in another disease involving harmful protein shapes would support wider use of the principle.

uncertain: How much function can return once harmful protein shapes are controlled, especially where cells have already been lost?
What size of functional gain and length of follow-up would establish meaningful, sustained recovery in each disease?
What additional evidence would show that removing or neutralizing the harmful shape caused recovery?

page.title: Protein aggregate clearance with functional recovery
page.definition: A drug removes established aggregates of misfolded proteins from human tissue or neutralizes their harmful activity. Patients regain function they had lost before treatment, and the improvement persists. In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, imaging estimates of heart deposits fell and patients reported better health during an open-label cliramitug extension. The absence of a concurrent control leaves the cause of those gains uncertain.

goal.need: An estimated 7.4 million Americans aged 65 or older had clinical Alzheimer’s dementia in 2026. In early disease, patients receiving lecanemab still lost cognitive and everyday function, though more slowly. In light-chain amyloidosis, heart or kidney dysfunction can persist after abnormal protein production falls. In transthyretin cardiomyopathy, drugs that limit new deposits leave existing ones in place. Where damage is reversible, recovery could mean walking or showering with less help. Irreversible organ damage may still require transplantation.

figures.caption: Anti-amyloid antibodies versus placebo at 18 months in early Alzheimer’s disease.
figures.note: Negative values favour treatment. Standardized mean differences express effects in standard-deviation units.

statements.quote: Reducing myocardial ATTR load is a therapeutic goal anticipated to translate into restored cardiac function
statements.context: ATTR denotes transthyretin amyloid. The passage states the intended consequence of removing cardiac deposits.

statements.quote: This has the potential to be the first treatment for AL amyloidosis that could restore organ function.
statements.context: A horizon-scanning assessment of investigational NEOD001, describing its intended capability rather than established efficacy. AL denotes immunoglobulin light-chain amyloidosis.

statements.quote: remove existing amyloid deposits to potentially limit and reverse organ dysfunction.
statements.context: Appendix 6 of The Voice of the Patient Report identifies this aim alongside suppression of amyloid-forming light chains and supportive care for affected organs.

statements.quote: Future research on disease-modifying treatments for Alzheimer’s disease should focus on other mechanisms of action.
statements.context: The review judged the cognitive and dementia-severity effects of amyloid-β antibodies trivial at 18 months and the functional effects small at best in people with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease.

completion.title: A controlled trial demonstrates aggregate clearance or neutralization with sustained functional recovery.
completion.criterion: In patients with established protein-aggregation disease, a randomized controlled trial demonstrates removal or loss of pathogenic activity of the targeted aggregates alongside clinically meaningful improvement above pretreatment patient function. The gain must exceed control and persist to the protocol’s final efficacy assessment, using a published disease-specific meaningful-change criterion and a justified measure of the targeted pathological state. Reduced decline or a biomarker response alone does not qualify. No common numerical recovery magnitude or duration is specified by the cited bodies.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; synthesis of the cited developers’ goals, not an established regulatory or society criterion.
completion.basis: Searches of FDA/EMA guidance, Amyloidosis Forum and TRAC frameworks, and NI006-101, coramitug, CARES and Clarity AD protocols/results found no combined clearance-and-restoration criterion or common recovery magnitude and duration. This test combines the developers’ removal and recovery goals while distinguishing restoration from biomarker responses and reduced decline.

milestones.title: A drug reduces pre-existing protein aggregates in a controlled animal experiment.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate less pre-existing aggregate in treated animals than in controls using the published tissue assay. In the transthyretin protocol, compare the immunostained amyloid area in mice grafted with patient-derived fibrils after treatment with the test antibody or an isotype-matched control. The protocol assesses grafts at 6 and 96 hours.
milestones.set_by: Neurimmune, Michalon et al., Figure 6 and animal methods; this published assay concerns transthyretin amyloid grafts.
milestones.threshold_quote: ATTR remaining after 6 and 96 h of treatment was detected by IHC staining and quantified

milestones.title: A human dose meets the trial’s tolerability criteria for further study.
milestones.criterion: Identify a dose for further study under the trial’s dose-selection rules. In light-chain amyloidosis, NEOD001 defined the maximum tolerated dose as the highest dose at which at most one of six patients had a dose-limiting toxicity during month one. If that maximum was not reached, the protocol allowed selection up to the highest tested dose using toxicity and biological, pharmacological and clinical activity. In transthyretin cardiomyopathy, NI006 guided escalation by adverse events, laboratory tests, echocardiography and electrocardiography.
milestones.set_by: Prothena NEOD001 protocol NCT01707264 and NI006 protocol NCT04360434. The one-in-six rule belongs to NEOD001.
milestones.threshold_quote: the highest dose level at which no more than one of six patients experienced a DLT during the first month of therapy

milestones.title: An aggregate-targeting drug produces a disease-specific imaging response in people with established deposits.
milestones.criterion: Show a treatment-related reduction from baseline on an imaging measure of established deposits. For cerebral amyloid-β, partial treatment-related amyloid clearance requires a PET decline exceeding test–retest and measurement variability while the scan remains positive. Full clearance on PET requires a fall below the predetermined positivity threshold. For systemic deposits, use the organ-specific protocol, such as radiolabeled serum amyloid P scintigraphy for hepatic amyloid or cardiac tracer uptake or MRI extracellular volume for myocardial transthyretin amyloid.
milestones.set_by: Alzheimer’s Association-convened TRAC workgroup, 2025; its definition concerns cerebral amyloid-β. The cited systemic-amyloidosis studies use different imaging protocols.
milestones.threshold_quote: Partial TRAC means that PET levels dropped significantly but remain above threshold.

milestones.title: An aggregate-targeting drug produces a meaningful improvement in patient-reported health status.
milestones.criterion: Show that a patient’s health-status score improves from pretreatment baseline by a published meaningful-change threshold for the instrument. The NI006-101 transthyretin cardiomyopathy follow-up compared each participant’s Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score at the end of the second open-label extension with baseline and counted a gain of at least 5 points as meaningful.
milestones.set_by: NI006-101 investigators, 2026 follow-up, applying the questionnaire’s 5-point convention. The Amyloidosis Forum reports limited evidence validating meaningful-change thresholds in transthyretin cardiomyopathy.
milestones.threshold_quote: improvements above clinically meaningful threshold (≥5 points)

milestones.title: An aggregate-targeting drug meets its prespecified primary clinical efficacy test in a randomized phase 3 trial.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate benefit over control on the protocol’s primary clinical endpoint in the prespecified analysis population, using its significance level and multiplicity rules. In Clarity AD, the test compares 18-month change in Clinical Dementia Rating–Sum of Boxes between treatment and placebo at two-sided α = 0.05. In light-chain amyloidosis, CARES uses a hierarchical composite of time to death from any cause and frequency of cardiovascular hospitalizations. Either endpoint permits benefit while patients continue to lose function.
milestones.set_by: Clarity AD protocol NCT03887455 and CARES protocols NCT04512235 and NCT04504825.
milestones.threshold_quote: Each test was performed at an alpha level of 0.05 (two-sided)

milestones.title: A drug reduces the toxicity of preformed aggregates in a controlled cell assay.
milestones.criterion: Expose cells to aggregates formed before drug treatment and demonstrate less toxicity than with the control preparation. In the amyloid-β assay, incubate preformed fibrils with the test antibody or an unrelated antibody for 24 hours. After 48 hours of exposure, compare the ability of PC 12 cells to reduce the dye MTT, a measure of cellular metabolic activity.
milestones.set_by: Solomon and colleagues, published amyloid-β cytotoxicity assay, Figure 5.
milestones.threshold_quote: preformed β-amyloid (2.5 μM) incubated for a further 24 h with mAb 6C6

not_found: No cross-proteinopathy numerical threshold or required follow-up duration combining aggregate clearance with functional recovery was found.
No cross-disease validated test for neutralization of pathogenic aggregates remaining in tissue was found.
No randomized demonstration satisfying the combined completion test was identified among the cited human studies.

results.finding: With higher-dose NI006 for ATTR cardiomyopathy, median cardiac MRI extracellular volume fell 17.8 percentage points from baseline to month 12 in 3 patients.
results.detail: The 17.8-point figure is the difference between reported medians. The MRI and scintigraphy measures are surrogates for myocardial amyloid load, and fewer patients had 12-month imaging.

A total of 48 ± 4% of plaques disappeared after
ch
aducanumab treatment compared with only 14 ± 3% of plaques disappearing after treatment with a control antibody, P1.17

results.finding: In mice with human ALκ amyloidomas (7 per group), 2A4 lowered mean residual graft weight by 65% versus JH70.
results.detail: The 65% difference is calculated from the reported group means. The 6- and 96-hour assessments are specific to the transthyretin protocol.
results.quote: Treatment with 2A4 expedited regression of ALκ amyloidomas in mice, likely mediated by the action of macrophages and neutrophils, relative to animals that received a control antibody.

results.finding: In phase Ib, crenezumab 60 mg/kg IV every 4 weeks (n=21) was selected for phase III based on interim safety data.
results.detail: The randomized phase also tested 120 mg/kg. The protocol switched that cohort to 60 mg/kg in the open-label extension.
results.quote: Overall, most AEs were low grade and no protocol-defined dose-limiting toxicities or deaths occurred.

results.finding: In amyloid-positive Alzheimer’s disease, PET SUVR may have stabilized in the 60 participants across the two higher-dose crenezumab groups.
results.detail: All follow-up PET comparisons occurred during the open-label extension without a concurrent placebo group. The study was underpowered for imaging comparisons and reported no numerical SUVR change in the supplied prose.
results.quote: participants who received the higher doses (45 and 60 mg/kg IV q4w) may have stabilized SUVR over time, whereas mean SUVR in participants in the lowest dose group (30 mg/kg IV q4w) increased

results.finding: PRX004 dose escalation in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (n=21) recorded 0 dose-limiting toxicities.
results.detail: The report identifies 30 mg/kg as the highest tested dose and describes all tested doses as well tolerated.
results.quote:
There were no drug-related serious AEs, dose-limiting 
toxicities, or deaths

results.finding: In the Alzheimer trial (n=1,736 randomized), 76.4% of donanemab-treated participants reached PET-defined amyloid clearance at week 76.
results.detail: The trial required at least 37 Centiloids on screening PET and defined amyloid clearance as less than 24.1 Centiloids.
results.quote: In the combined population, amyloid clearance was reached in 29.7% (95% CI, 26.56%-33.04%) of participants at 24 weeks and 76.4% (95% CI, 72.87%-79.57%) at 76 weeks of donanemab-treated participants compared with 0.2% (95% CI, 0.07%-0.90%) at 24 weeks and 0.3% (95% CI, 0.08%-1.05%) at 76 weeks of placebo-treated participants

results.finding: In the Alzheimer phase 3 trial (n=1,736 randomized), donanemab favored placebo by 2.92 iADRS points in the combined population at week 76.
results.detail: The combined primary analysis used 775 donanemab and 824 placebo participants with baseline and at least one postbaseline efficacy measurement. Mean iADRS scores declined from baseline in both groups.

results.finding: In the trontinemab open-label extension (n=126), five participants withdrew from treatment because of adverse events.
results.detail: Safety outcomes were grouped by previous treatment and amyloid PET status at extension baseline. Some participants received both doses.

results.finding: Among 59 participants with week-28 scans on trontinemab 3.6 mg/kg, 92% reached the prespecified PET-negative range.
results.quote: 92% of participants were below the amyloid positivity threshold at 28 weeks†,‡

results.finding: The AT-02 AL extension enrolled 14 participants and advanced the 2500 mg every-two-weeks regimen to renal expansion.
results.detail: The safety summary covers both dosing schedules.
results.quote:
• Expansion renal  cohort  recruitment  is underway.  Patients  with  impaired eGFR and/or  proteinuria 
will receive 2500 mg of AT02 bi-weekly for  24 weeks.

results.finding: In one AT-02-treated participant with AL amyloidosis, left ventricular septal AT-01 PET uptake fell 14%.
results.detail: This exploratory paired-scan result comes from one participant. Its attribution to AT-02 remains uncertain.

results.finding: One AT-02-treated participant with AL amyloidosis gained 22.2 KCCQ Overall Summary Score points from baseline to week 24.
results.detail: The individual result is from the open-label extension. The report does not give a cohort-wide count meeting the 5-point threshold.

results.finding: In ATTR-grafted mice (4–5 per group), ch.NI301A reduced immunostained graft area by 50.9 percentage points versus isotype control.
results.detail: The 50.9-percentage-point difference was measured at 96 hours with 5 mg/kg of the mouse-chimeric antibody. Graft amyloid also declined spontaneously in the isotype-control group.
results.quote: Both the 5 and 50 mg/kg doses removed the amyloid fibrils almost completely, down to background levels of about 7% of the graft area.

results.finding: In the 698-person Clarity AD PET substudy, lecanemab reduced brain amyloid by 59.12 centiloids relative to placebo.
results.detail: The threshold comparison applies to the treated group mean.
results.quote:
The adjusted mean 
change from baseline at 18 months was −55.48 
centiloids in the lecanemab group and 3.64 cen-
tiloids in the placebo group (difference, −59.12 
centiloids; 95% CI, −62.64 to −55.60; P<0.001)

results.finding: In the 1,734-person Clarity AD efficacy population, lecanemab reduced 18-month CDR-SB worsening by 0.45 points versus placebo.
results.quote:
The adjusted least-squares mean change from baseline at 18 
months was 1.21 with lecanemab and 1.66 with placebo (difference, −0.45; 95% 
confidence interval [CI], −0.67 to −0.23; P<0.001).

results.finding: In the ABBV-916 trial (106 randomized), safety review led to down-titration of the highest-dose cohort (n=13) to 900 mg.
results.detail: The sponsor discontinued the trial before Stage B because it deprioritized the program.
results.quote: The 3000 mg dose was reduced to 2000 mg and subsequently to 900 mg after safety review.

results.finding: Among early Alzheimer’s patients with week-24 PET in the fixed 900 mg ABBV-916 cohorts (n=12), 100% reached amyloid negativity.
results.detail: The fixed 900 mg cohorts enrolled 28 patients. The week-24 negativity percentage applies to the 12 with evaluable scans at that visit.
results.quote: Although the down‐titrated 2000/900 mg cohort achieved a lower rate of amyloid negativity at week 24 (71.4%; 5/7) compared to the 900 mg cohort (100%; 12/12), despite greater overall drug exposure, this finding should be interpreted with caution, given the small sample size.

results.finding: In mice with patient-derived transthyretin amyloid grafts (4–5 per group), ch.NI301A reduced immunostained amyloid area by 50.9 percentage points versus isotype control.
results.detail: The isotype control group also showed spontaneous graft amyloid loss by 96 hours. The reported effect is the additional reduction versus that concurrent control.
results.quote: All three doses (0.5, 5, and 50 mg/kg body weight) of ch.NI301A further reduced ATTR in a dose-dependent manner.

results.finding: In 698 Clarity AD PET substudy participants, lecanemab reduced brain amyloid by 59.12 centiloids relative to placebo at 18 months.
results.detail: The lecanemab group’s mean PET amyloid burden reached 22.99 centiloids. Threshold crossing applies to the group mean. The proportion of individual scans that became negative is undetermined.
results.quote:
The adjusted mean 
change from baseline at 18 months was −55.48 
centiloids in the lecanemab group and 3.64 cen-
til oids in the placebo group (difference, −59.12 
centiloids; 95% CI, −62.64 to −55.60; P<0.001) (Fig. 2B and Table 2).

results.finding: In 1,734 Clarity AD participants, lecanemab reduced 18-month CDR-SB worsening by 0.45 points versus placebo.
In SH-SY5Y cells exposed to preformed TTR oligomers, Ab-A increased viability by 37.3% versus PBS (quadruplicate measurements).
results.detail: The separate cell assay with mature TTR fibrils and control IgG measured microglial uptake only.
results.quote: Compared to PBS, cell viability was increased by 3.3% ± 2.1, 8.8% ± 4.9, 20.6% ± 6.2 and 37.3% ± 0.3, respectively.

results.finding: Tet-off APP mice given Ab9 plus doxycycline had about 72% less cortical amyloid area than IgG plus doxycycline controls (n=14 per group).
results.detail: The reduction chiefly affected diffuse amyloid. Thioflavine-S-positive fibrillar burden did not change significantly in the younger cohort.
results.quote: Dox + Ab9 intervention at both 6 and 18 mo yielded an equivalent 72% reduction in amyloid load compared to dox + IgG, but because the 18 mo mice started treatment with less amyloid, they ended with almost none.

results.finding: Phase I NI006 in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (sample size unstated) reached 60 mg/kg every four weeks without dose-limiting toxicity.
results.detail: The 0.3 mg/kg dose was selected before human dosing as the first-in-human starting dose.
results.quote: overall, no dose‐limiting toxicities were observed up to the highest dose tested (60 mg/kg Q4W).

results.finding: Anselamimab 1,000 mg/m² was selected for phase III in systemic AL amyloidosis after 0 dose-limiting toxicities among 6 patients at that dose.
results.detail: The 13-patient dose-escalation cohort received 500, 750 or 1,000 mg/m². The protocol defined dose-limiting toxicity as a treatment-related adverse reaction of CTCAE grade 3 or higher.
results.quote:
パート A の DLT評価期において、13例（500 mg/m2 投与 4 例、750 mg/m2 投与 3 例、1,000 mg/m2投与
6 例）全例で DLT20）は認められなかったことから、本薬の第 III相試験の検討用量として 1,000 mg/m2が
選択された。

results.finding: In early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease, 37.9% of donanemab recipients with evaluable PET (n = 66) reached amyloid plaque clearance at 6 months.
results.detail: The phase 3 trial was open-label, with PET readers blinded to treatment assignment.
results.quote: In the overall population, 37.9% (25 of 66) of donanemab‐treated participants versus 1.6% (1 of 64) of aducanumab‐treated participants reached AP clearance at 6 months ( P  < 0.001; Figure  2A ).

results.finding: In cliramitug-treated transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (n=8 with follow-up scintigraphy), median cardiac tracer uptake fell 36.1% from baseline.
results.detail: The extension analysis was descriptive, and 20 of 23 participants were receiving tafamidis at baseline.
results.quote: with a median (IQR) absolute reduction of −2.2% (−1.3 to −2.8) and median (IQR) relative reduction of −36.1% (−25.9 to −45.7) from baseline.

results.finding: With cliramitug, 13 of 22 evaluable patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy gained ≥5 points on the KCCQ Overall Summary Score.
results.detail: For participants initially assigned placebo, baseline was the last assessment before the first open-label extension. The second extension had no concurrent control, and 20 of 23 enrollees were on background tafamidis at baseline.
results.quote: including 13 patients with improvements above clinically meaningful threshold (≥5 points)

results.finding: κ-type AL amyloidosis patients receiving anselamimab (n=28 evaluable) gained a mean 18.5 KCCQ-OS points from baseline at week 50.
results.detail: Table 45 reports a secondary outcome based on available week-50 scores from a subgroup. The confidence interval for the between-group difference includes zero.

definition = "A drug removes established aggregates of misfolded proteins from human tissue or neutralizes their harmful activity. Patients regain function they had lost before treatment, and the improvement persists. In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, imaging estimates of heart deposits fell and patients reported better health during an open-label cliramitug extension. The absence of a concurrent control leaves the cause of those gains uncertain.". Reason: The definition gains a concrete example of how close human studies have come and what the uncontrolled follow-up leaves unresolved.

goal.need = "An estimated 7.4 million Americans aged 65 or older had clinical Alzheimer\u2019s dementia in 2026. In early disease, patients receiving lecanemab still lost cognitive and everyday function, though more slowly. In light-chain amyloidosis, heart or kidney dysfunction can persist after abnormal protein production falls. In transthyretin cardiomyopathy, drugs that limit new deposits leave existing ones in place. Where damage is reversible, recovery could mean walking or showering with less help. Irreversible organ damage may still require transplantation.". Reason: The current rationale reports trial results but omits the scale of the burden, the everyday abilities patients could regain and the limit imposed by irreversible organ damage.

add statement by Amyloidosis Research Consortium, 2016: "remove existing amyloid deposits to potentially limit and reverse organ dysfunction.". Reason: The patient consortium explicitly linked removal of existing light-chain deposits to reversal of organ dysfunction before the two statements already listed.

add statement by Cochrane review authors, 2026: "Future research on disease-modifying treatments for Alzheimer’s disease should focus on other mechanisms of action.". Reason: The Cochrane review gives a contrary assessment specific to amyloid-β removal in early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease.

add milestone after None: "A drug reduces the toxicity of preformed aggregates in a controlled cell assay.". Reason: A controlled cell assay captures the early laboratory demonstration that treatment can reduce the harmful activity of aggregates formed before exposure to the drug.

edit m1: criterion = "Demonstrate less pre-existing aggregate in treated animals than in controls using the published tissue assay. In the transthyretin protocol, compare the immunostained amyloid area in mice grafted with patient-derived fibrils after treatment with the test antibody or an isotype-matched control. The protocol assesses grafts at 6 and 96 hours."; threshold_quote = "ATTR remaining after 6 and 96\u2009h of treatment was detected by IHC staining and quantified"; threshold_ref = 3; refs = [3]. Reason: The animal criterion currently reports successful doses alongside the test for removal of preformed material.

edit m2: title = "A human dose meets the trial\u2019s tolerability criteria for further study."; criterion = "Identify a dose for further study under the trial\u2019s dose-selection rules. In light-chain amyloidosis, NEOD001 defined the maximum tolerated dose as the highest dose at which at most one of six patients had a dose-limiting toxicity during month one. If that maximum was not reached, the protocol allowed selection up to the highest tested dose using toxicity and biological, pharmacological and clinical activity. In transthyretin cardiomyopathy, NI006 guided escalation by adverse events, laboratory tests, echocardiography and electrocardiography."; set_by = "Prothena NEOD001 protocol NCT01707264 and NI006 protocol NCT04360434. The one-in-six rule belongs to NEOD001."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "the highest dose level at which no more than one of six patients experienced a DLT during the first month of therapy"; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7, 9]. Reason: The one-in-six rule defined the maximum tolerated dose in NEOD001, while the protocol separately allowed selection of a dose for further study when that maximum was not reached.

edit m3: criterion = "Show a treatment-related reduction from baseline on an imaging measure of established deposits. For cerebral amyloid-\u03b2, partial treatment-related amyloid clearance requires a PET decline exceeding test\u2013retest and measurement variability while the scan remains positive. Full clearance on PET requires a fall below the predetermined positivity threshold. For systemic deposits, use the organ-specific protocol, such as radiolabeled serum amyloid P scintigraphy for hepatic amyloid or cardiac tracer uptake or MRI extracellular volume for myocardial transthyretin amyloid."; threshold_quote = "Partial TRAC means that PET levels dropped significantly but remain above threshold."; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6, 8, 9]. Reason: The imaging criterion mixes observed response rates with its threshold and omits the test–retest variability that distinguishes partial brain amyloid clearance from measurement noise.

edit m4: criterion = "Show that a patient\u2019s health-status score improves from pretreatment baseline by a published meaningful-change threshold for the instrument. The NI006-101 transthyretin cardiomyopathy follow-up compared each participant\u2019s Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score at the end of the second open-label extension with baseline and counted a gain of at least 5 points as meaningful."; set_by = "NI006-101 investigators, 2026 follow-up, applying the questionnaire\u2019s 5-point convention. The Amyloidosis Forum reports limited evidence validating meaningful-change thresholds in transthyretin cardiomyopathy."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "improvements above clinically meaningful threshold (\u22655 points)"; threshold_ref = 11; refs = [11, 5]. Reason: The participant counts and organ biomarker responses obscure the within-patient questionnaire change that this milestone tests.

edit m5: title = "An aggregate-targeting drug meets its prespecified primary clinical efficacy test in a randomized phase 3 trial."; criterion = "Demonstrate benefit over control on the protocol\u2019s primary clinical endpoint in the prespecified analysis population, using its significance level and multiplicity rules. In Clarity AD, the test compares 18-month change in Clinical Dementia Rating\u2013Sum of Boxes between treatment and placebo at two-sided \u03b1 = 0.05. In light-chain amyloidosis, CARES uses a hierarchical composite of time to death from any cause and frequency of cardiovascular hospitalizations. Either endpoint permits benefit while patients continue to lose function."; set_by = "Clarity AD protocol NCT03887455 and CARES protocols NCT04512235 and NCT04504825."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "Each test was performed at an alpha level of 0.05 (two-sided)"; threshold_ref = 10; refs = [10, 12]. Reason: The phase 3 criterion mixes the prespecified efficacy test with trial results, a subgroup finding and a recruitment-status update.
